Feluda.description: The main detective, Prodosh C. Mitter, known for his sharp intellect and investigative skills.

Aniruddha Haldar.description: The six-year-old son of Amitabh Haldar who owns a toy machine-gun and asks Feluda to find his missing bird.

Amitabh Haldar.description: Aniruddha's father, son of Parvaticharan Haldar, who invites Feluda to their home.

Parvaticharan Haldar.description: A retired barrister and passionate collector of antiques, father of Amitabh, and the murder victim found dead in his study.

Lalmohan Babu.description: A writer of thrillers and Feluda's friend, known by his pen name Jatayu and real surname Ganguli.

Hrishikesh Datta.description: The current secretary of Parvaticharan Haldar and associate who arranges meetings and provides information about Barasat.

Charminar.description: A popular Indian cigarette brand, often associated with Feluda.

Hobby Centre.description: A shop located at the corner of Park Street and Russell Street, selling toys and other items.

Park Street.description: A well-known street in Kolkata, famous for its shops and restaurants.

Russell Street.description: A street in Kolkata intersecting with Park Street.

Uncle Sidhu.description: A recurring character in the Feluda stories, known for his knowledge and age.

Barasat.description: A town near Kolkata where the Haldar family resides.

New Market.description: A historic and popular shopping area in Kolkata.

Tinkori Babu.description: The owner of a well-known pet shop in New Market.

Mughal.description: Refers to the Mughal Empire, an important historical period in India.

Warren Hastings.description: The first Governor-General of India under British rule.

Napoleon.description: Refers to Napoleon Bonaparte, the French military leader and emperor.

VIP Road.description: A major road in Kolkata connecting the city to the airport.

Bagbazar.description: A neighborhood in Kolkata, known for its sweet shops.

Calcutta.description: The former name of Kolkata, a major city in India.

Sai Baba.description: A revered spiritual leader in India, with many followers and ashrams.

chandana.description: A type of bird, commonly kept as a pet in Bengal.

kachauris.description: A popular Indian snack, deep-fried and stuffed with spiced filling.

Baba.description: A common Indian term for father.

ashram.description: A spiritual hermitage or monastery in Indian religions.

chowkidar.description: A watchman or security guard, especially in Indian households.

supari.description: Areca nut, often chewed in India and also refers to the tree it grows on.

Durga Puja.description: A major Hindu festival celebrated in Bengal and other parts of India.

Inspector Hajra.description: The police inspector in charge of the case, who respects Feluda.

Achintya Haldar.description: Amitabh’s younger brother and Aniruddha's uncle, involved in theatre and a potential suspect in the Haldar family mystery.

Nobo Rangamanch.description: A theatre company in Calcutta where Achintya Haldar seeks work.

Alkathene.description: A type of plastic (polyethylene) commonly used for making envelopes and containers in India.

Sadhan Dastidar.description: Parvaticharan's former secretary, known for his superstitious nature and mysterious disappearance.

Mukundo.description: Mukundo is a bearer (servant) in the Haldar household, responsible for serving coffee.

Haldar.description: The Haldar family, central to the story, whose house is the site of the murder and theft.

Lord Sinha Road.description: A street in Kolkata, mentioned as the location of a clinic visited by Pestonji.

Bowbazar Street.description: A street in Kolkata, referenced as the address of the ancient Parsi household.

Parsi.description: Parsi refers to the Zoroastrian community in India, originally from Persia, with a long history in Kolkata.

Siraj-ud-daula.description: Siraj-ud-daula was the last independent Nawab of Bengal, referenced in relation to the history of Parsis in Calcutta.

Jai Guru.description: A spiritual phrase, often used in Indian religious contexts, meaning 'Victory to the Guru'.

Hare Krishna.description: A Hindu devotional chant associated with the worship of Lord Krishna.

babu.description: A respectful term for a gentleman, commonly used in Bengal and northern India.

mali.description: A gardener, responsible for tending to plants and gardens.

bearer.description: A household servant, often responsible for serving food and drinks.

telegram.description: A message sent via telegraph, once a common method of communication in India.

Topshe.description: Feluda's cousin and assistant, who narrates the story and helps with investigations.

R.D. Pestonji.description: An elderly antiquarian and collector interested in buying the stolen Napoleon letter.

Abhilash Poddar.description: The proprietor of Nobo Rangamanch theatre on Cornwallis Street.

Manas Banerjee.description: An actor mentioned as one of the leading men at the theatre.

Srinath.description: A servant who brings coffee to guests in Feluda's house.

Boubazar.description: A locality in Calcutta (Kolkata), known for its old houses and bustling streets.

St Helena.description: An island in the South Atlantic where Napoleon was exiled after his defeat.

Zurich.description: A city in Switzerland, mentioned as the place where the Napoleon letter was bought.

Ming.description: Refers to the Ming dynasty of China, known for its exquisite porcelain vases.

Cornwallis Street.description: A street in Calcutta, location of the Nobo Rangamanch theatre.

Bombay.description: The former name of Mumbai, a major city in western India.

Bahadur Shah Zafar.description: The last Mughal emperor of India, referenced as the original owner of a snuff box.

Madhumurali Deeghi.description: A lake near the broken indigo factory, mentioned as a meeting place.

Rajasthan.description: A state in western India, known for its history of dacoits (bandits).

paan.description: A preparation combining betel leaf with areca nut and sometimes tobacco, chewed for its stimulant effects.

attar.description: A fragrant essential oil, usually derived from flowers, used as perfume.

biriyani.description: A popular Indian rice dish cooked with spices, meat, or vegetables.

dacoits.description: Armed bandits or robbers, especially those operating in rural India.

Sadhu.description: A term meaning 'holy man' or ascetic, but here used as a nickname.

Haripada.description: Lalmohan Babu’s enthusiastic driver, who admires Feluda and assists the group.

Mrs Haldar.description: Amitabh Haldar’s wife, who helps make arrangements for the guests.

Colt.description: A brand of revolver, indicating Feluda is armed with a firearm.

sheora.description: A type of tree (Streblus asper), often associated with folklore and ghost stories in Bengal.

aloo-sabzi.description: A spiced potato curry, commonly served as a side dish with Indian breads.

veranda.description: A roofed, open-air gallery or porch attached to the outside of a building, common in Indian architecture.

Odomos.description: A popular Indian brand of mosquito repellent cream.

rickshaw.description: A small, two- or three-wheeled passenger vehicle, commonly used for transport in India.

goondas.description: A Hindi word for hired thugs or hooligans, often involved in criminal activities.

Shankar.description: The son of the mali (gardener), known for his skill in catching birds.

Radhe Shyam.description: A traditional Hindu greeting or chant, often used in devotional contexts.

dadu.description: A Bengali term meaning grandfather, used affectionately by children.
